Federal Reserve · 9 August 2011

How the Fed’s rate hold moved the yield curve

The Fed held its target at 0–0.25% and said exceptionally low rates would probably be warranted through at least mid-2013. Both Treasury yields fell. Whether the curve steepened or flattened depends on when you stopped the clock.

US Treasury yield changes
InstrumentStatement windowFull day
2-year Treasury−9.52 bp≈ −10 bp
10-year Treasury−2.42 bp≈ −20 bp
10-year minus 2-year+7.10 bp≈ −10 bp

The San Francisco Fed window runs from 10 minutes before to 20 minutes after the statement. Full-day changes are Fed staff estimates. The spread change is calculated from the two yields in each column.

What investors repriced

The two-year yield fell further than the ten-year in the statement window. Interest-rate cap prices also put the expected first tightening two quarters later, moving it from Q2 to Q4 2013. By the end of the day the larger decline was in the ten-year yield.

Commitment or a weaker outlook?

A commitment to hold rates low for a given outlook reduces expected borrowing costs. A downgrade to the outlook can also push an expected hike further away, even if the committee would respond to any given level of growth and inflation exactly as before. The distinction matters for equities because weaker expected earnings can offset a lower discount rate.

What to check next

Compare policy futures or overnight index swaps for meetings inside and beyond the guidance horizon. Check subsequent responses to comparable growth releases. A credible commitment can dampen repricing inside that horizon. Falling rates alongside weakening growth forecasts give the outlook channel more weight.

Limits of the evidence

The full-day figures are approximate and include trading outside the release window. Both policy guidance and the Fed’s assessment of the economy arrived in the same statement, so even intraday prices cannot identify their separate effects.

Sources
  • Federal Open Market Committee. FOMC statement. 9 August 2011 · Economic assessment and policy decision
  • Federal Reserve staff. Tealbook B, Forward Rate Guidance and Policy Expectations. 19 January 2012 · printed pp. 20–21
  • Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco. U.S. Monetary Policy Event-Study Database. Statements sheet, 9 August 2011. Interest-rate changes converted from percentage points to basis points.
  • Miguel Acosta et al. Financial Market Effects of FOMC Communication. Definition of the statement window, section 2.2

United States · July–October 2023

Why the ten-year yield rose towards the end of the hiking cycle

Between early July and late October 2023, the ten-year Treasury yield rose by more than a percentage point. Did investors expect the Fed to hold rates higher, or did they want more compensation for owning long bonds?

What the market and the issuer reported
ObservationPeriodReading
10-year Treasury yieldEarly July–end October 2023Rise of more than 100 bp
Net borrowing estimate31 July revision for July–SeptemberUp $274bn from the May estimate

Treasury’s revision covers privately held net marketable borrowing across maturities. It gives no direct measure of the extra interest-rate risk issued to investors.

How supply reaches the long end

A ten-year yield reflects expected short rates over the bond’s life and the compensation investors require for bearing interest-rate risk. When private investors must hold more long-dated debt, they may demand a higher yield even if their view of the next few Fed meetings barely changes. The maturity mix matters because issuing bills adds far less duration than issuing long bonds.

What the models found

In November, the New York Fed’s markets manager reported that the models his team monitored attributed most of the July–October rise to the term premium on average. A later Fed staff study also pointed to quantitative tightening and uncertainty alongside greater issuance.

How to test that reading

Around a refunding announcement, compare the ten-year yield with the two-year yield and meeting-dated overnight index swaps. A long-end sell-off with little change in the next few meetings makes a duration explanation worth testing against announced coupon auction sizes and daily term-premium estimates. Broad repricing of meeting rates points to a policy-path contribution.

Limits of the evidence

Term premia are inferred from models. Daily model estimates cannot resolve a 15-minute event. Strong data and policy communication also moved yields over these months, and total borrowing alone does not identify how much duration investors absorbed.

Sources
  • US Department of the Treasury. Treasury Announces Marketable Borrowing Estimates. 31 July 2023 · July–September borrowing estimate
  • Roberto Perli, Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Disentangling Messages from the Treasury Market. 16 November 2023 · Panel 2 and accompanying text
  • Anthony M. Diercks and Dev Asnani. The Treasury Tantrum of 2023. 3 September 2024 · Executive summary and yield decomposition
  • Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Treasury Term Premia. Adrian–Crump–Moench daily and monthly model estimates

Japan · December 1931–November 1932

Japan leaves gold. Which exchange rate measures the move?

In December 1931 Japan restricted gold exports and the conversion of banknotes into gold. Once investors could no longer enforce the old gold parity, the yen had room to fall. The size of that fall depended on which currency the investor held.

Change in the foreign-currency value of one yen
AgainstDecember 1931–November 1932
US dollar−60%
Pound sterling−44%

The Bank of Japan Review reports the depreciation of the yen. Sterling had already left gold, so it provided a different benchmark from the US dollar.

From exchange rates to output

A weaker yen raised the yen value of overseas sales and gave exporters room to cut foreign-currency prices. Domestic demand also received support. The Bank of Japan cut its discount rate in March, June and August 1932. The government expanded spending on rural relief and military operations in Manchuria, and the Bank began underwriting government bonds on 25 November 1932.

How to read the sequence

Industrial production and wholesale prices were up year on year in 1932. To evaluate the recovery, line up exchange rates and export volumes with the timing of rate cuts, budget decisions and the first bond underwriting.

Limits of the evidence

The currency moved before the first central-bank bond underwriting. Fiscal announcements and rate cuts also preceded the purchase. Annual output data cannot isolate what each measure contributed to the recovery.

Sources
  • National Archives of Japan. Cabinet record on restrictions on gold convertibility (Japanese). 1931-12-13
  • Masato Shizume, Bank of Japan Review. The Japanese Economy during the Interwar Period. 2009-05 · pp. 6–7, chart 6

United Kingdom · 16–17 September 1992

Why a promised 15% rate failed to defend sterling

On 16 September sterling stayed at the floor of its European Exchange Rate Mechanism band. The authorities’ successive announcements show how a rate quoted in the news can differ from the rate borrowers actually face.

The sequence of the defence
UK policy announcementOutcome
16 September · Minimum lending rate raised to 12%Sterling remained at its floor.
16 September · 15% announced for the next dayThe Chancellor suspended participation that evening and rescinded the rise.

The Bank of England’s quarterly account records both announcements and the suspension. The announced 15% rate never took effect.

Why a higher rate could weaken confidence

Germany’s post-reunification inflation pressures kept German rates high while UK activity was weak. Defending sterling required high UK rates even as domestic inflation eased. A higher rate could reward holders of sterling, yet the extra burden on borrowers also raised the political cost of maintaining the peg.

The next morning’s gilt market

Compare sterling against the Deutsche Mark with gilts across maturities. On 17 September the Bank reported strong demand for gilts up to ten years as the prospect of rate cuts improved. Longer conventional gilts fell as inflation concerns rose. A single long gilt yield would have missed how the expected policy path and inflation outlook had diverged.

Limits of the evidence

The Bank also offered to buy longer gilts against shorter ones that morning. The observed curve records both changing expectations and official market operations.

Sources
  • Bank of England. Operation of monetary policy, Quarterly Bulletin 1992 Q4. 1992-12-01 · pp. 382–383, 392–393

Federal Reserve · March 2008

What did dealers need to borrow in March 2008?

A dealer could hold a mortgage-backed security and still be short of the cash needed to settle that day. Two Fed facilities addressed that problem by lending different things. The distinction matters when reading a balance-sheet announcement.

What each facility delivered
FacilityWhat the dealer receivedTerm
Term Securities Lending FacilityTreasury securities against eligible collateral28 days
Primary Dealer Credit FacilityCash against eligible collateralOvernight

The Fed announced the securities-lending facility on 11 March and the credit facility on 16 March 2008.

Why collateral quality mattered

A dealer holding an eligible mortgage-backed security could borrow a Treasury for 28 days through the securities-lending facility, then pledge it to raise cash privately. The credit facility offered eligible dealers overnight cash directly against collateral. Both channels gave a dealer another way to meet a payment without selling into a falling market. That backstop could help dealers keep making markets when private funding became more expensive.

What the first auction revealed

At the first securities-lending auction on 27 March, dealers bid $86.1bn for $75bn of Treasuries. The clearing fee was 33 basis points at an annual rate. Compare auction demand with the gap between repo rates on Treasury and less liquid collateral. Together they show what dealers were willing to pay for better collateral and whether private funding became easier.

Limits of the evidence

Auction bids measure demand for the facility. Concurrent changes in risk and other Fed actions complicate estimates of its independent effect on funding spreads.

Sources
  • Federal Reserve Board. Announcement of the Term Securities Lending Facility. 2008-03-11
  • Federal Reserve Board. Announcement of the Primary Dealer Credit Facility. 2008-03-16
  • Federal Reserve Board. Term Securities Lending Facility, auction dates. 2010-02-05
  • Federal Open Market Committee. June 2008 meeting presentation materials, exhibit 27. 2008-06-25

External forecast · Published November 2026

What would bring a second Fed hike into view?

J.P. Morgan Asset Management expected a December 2026 hike, followed by a pause. A further March 2027 hike was a risk in its outlook if inflation proved persistent. The report gives two forecasts against which to test that judgement.

US assumptions in the year-ahead outlook
IndicatorForecastMeasurement period
Real GDP growth1.6%Q4 2026 to Q4 2027
Headline PCE inflation2.3%Year to Q4 2027

J.P. Morgan Asset Management, 2027 Year-Ahead Investment Outlook, pp. 3–5. Both numbers are projections made in November 2026.

Which kind of disinflation?

The forecast depends partly on lower energy prices and fading tariff effects. A fall in headline inflation driven by fuel would give the Fed different evidence about underlying pressure from a slowdown in wages and services prices.

What would change the call?

At each inflation release, compare headline and core PCE with the underlying services data. Around a Fed announcement, check whether the implied March policy rate changes relative to December. Record the observation time for each price.

Assumptions to revisit

House forecast. Q4 2026 was incomplete when the report appeared. The inflation measure is headline PCE.

Sources
  • J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Market Insights. 2027 Year-Ahead Investment Outlook: Finding Balance in a Moderating Economic Environment. November 2026 · 2–5

External forecast · Published November 2026

How could a Fed pause coexist with high long yields?

J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s year-ahead outlook paired an extended pause after tightening with elevated long-term yields. The two calls depend on different buyers and different parts of the curve.

US Treasury assumptions in the year-ahead outlook
Forecast variableJ.P. Morgan Asset Management’s assumption
10-year Treasury yield4.75–5.25% for much of 2027
Net privately held Treasury borrowingMore than $2tn during 2027

The yield range describes a conditional view for much of the year. The borrowing number covers a full year of issuance, including bills.

What a policy pause leaves open

A pause can steady expectations for near-term overnight rates. At longer maturities, investors must also decide what yield they require to hold duration as the Treasury and corporate borrowers compete for financing. The maturity mix matters: a dollar of bills supplies far less duration than a dollar of long bonds.

What to watch at refunding

Compare changes in meeting-dated rates with the 2s10s curve. If the long end sells off while front-end pricing barely moves, inspect the Treasury’s refunding announcement, auction outcomes and inflation compensation before attributing the move to the Fed.

Assumptions to revisit

The yield range is the firm’s conditional forecast. Its central case excludes recession and a renewed external inflation shock.

Sources
  • J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Market Insights. 2027 Year-Ahead Investment Outlook: Finding Balance in a Moderating Economic Environment. November 2026 · 5–7

Strategic assumptions · Published 19 October 2026

When does an investment boom lift potential output?

In its 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, J.P. Morgan Asset Management raised its estimate of average US real growth from 1.8% to 2.1%. Its horizon is ten to fifteen years. The year-ahead report’s 1.6% US forecast covers four quarters, so the difference between the two figures cannot measure an acceleration in 2027.

Average annual real GDP growth assumed over 10–15 years
Economy2027 edition
United States2.1%
Euro area1.7%
Japan1.0%

J.P. Morgan Asset Management, 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, Exhibit 1. Each row uses the same long horizon.

Where the growth would come from

Buying equipment raises capital per worker. Deploying it well can subsequently raise output from a given quantity of labour and capital. These channels can operate on different schedules: a power or construction bottleneck may raise costs long before productivity gains become broad enough to ease inflation pressure.

How to tell whether the gains spread

Track real equipment investment alongside output per hour and multifactor productivity over several years. If investment remains concentrated and productivity gains fail to spread beyond technology producers, reassess how much additional potential output to assume.

Assumptions to revisit

Strategic assumptions depend on technology adoption and countervailing demographic headwinds. Cross-country figures are long-horizon growth rates, with no implied sequence of meeting decisions.

Sources
  • J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Portfolio Insights. 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, 31st annual edition. 19 October 2026 · 18–19, exhibit 1; 26–31
